catalog.note: Catalog selections and search only affect the recorded results below. They never fill the calculator above, which uses only the dimensions and parameters you enter manually.

physicalCorrections.title: Physical build corrections (estimated)
physicalCorrections.stepOnePrompt: First, choose the spoke type that matches your hub.
physicalCorrections.guideAriaLabel: Measurement datum schematic for J-bend and straight-pull spokes
physicalCorrections.guideJDatumDescription: Place the caliper at the throat of the inside 90° bend; this is the effective length start.
physicalCorrections.guideThreadEndDescription: Finish at the flush end of the thread and include the complete rolled thread section.
physicalCorrections.guideThreadSectionDescription: The thread belongs to the spoke body, so do not stop the measurement early for the nipple.
physicalCorrections.guideJCapWarningDescription: Starting at the outside of the head includes bend thickness and makes the result too long.
physicalCorrections.guideJOuterArcWarningTitle: Outside arc is not a datum
physicalCorrections.guideJOuterArcWarningDescription: The cold-formed outside arc has shape tolerance and its tangent is not repeatable.
physicalCorrections.guideStraightDatumDescription: Start at the bearing shoulder below the head where it contacts the hub, then measure to the thread end.
physicalCorrections.guideStraightHeadWarningDescription: The head sits in the hub counterbore; measure only the effective section after the bearing face.
physicalCorrections.stepTwoPrompt: Enter rim ERD, rim offset, and alternating-drilling offset
physicalCorrections.stepTwoSubtitle: Enter the front and rear rim ERD, overall rim-bed offset, and alternating-hole offset. Measurement guidance and geometry diagrams follow below.
physicalCorrections.stepThreePrompt: Set rim hole count, lacing, and hub PCD / WL / WR
physicalCorrections.stepThreeSubtitle: Choose a rim-hole count and lacing topology for each wheel, then enter its hub PCD and left/right flange-to-centerline distances.
physicalCorrections.stepFourPrompt: Set flange-hole diameter and spoke-length corrections
physicalCorrections.stepFourSubtitle: Enter the front and rear hub flange-hole diameters, then set crossing interlacing and spoke-elongation corrections as needed.
physicalCorrections.stepFiveSubtitle: External nipples are the length datum; this calculator uses a 14 mm SAPIM POLYAX external nipple as the datum. When using an internal nipple, enter its actual length.
physicalCorrections.stepSixSubtitle: Calculate to view each side's spoke lengths, topology-group lengths, and predicted tension ratios for both wheels. Editing an input clears the previous results, so calculate again.
physicalCorrections.rimGeometryOffsetSubtitle: Enter the overall rim offset and the alternating left/right hole offset from the rim center reference.
physicalCorrections.holeStepSubtitle: Confirm the flange-hole diameter used to subtract the hole radius from the theoretical hole center; the measurement rule applies to both J-bend and straight-pull hubs.
physicalCorrections.interlacingStepSubtitle: Choose whether the spokes are interlaced at crossings and enter the spoke elongation correction used for cut length.
physicalCorrections.pcdPairHelp: Choose the rim-hole count and lacing topology separately for each wheel, then enter its hub PCD, WL, and WR.
physicalCorrections.flangeOrientationNote: Left and right follow the rider seated on the bicycle facing forward. Keep this orientation consistent with the hub maker's drawing.
physicalCorrections.frontFlangeSideNote: Left flange = disc side · Right flange = non-disc side
physicalCorrections.rearFlangeSideNote: Left flange = non-drive side (NDS) · Right flange = drive side (DS, freehub side)
physicalCorrections.alternatingPairHelp: Enter the front and rear alternating-drilling offsets separately; use 0 when the rim has no alternating drilling.
physicalCorrections.alternatingInputNote: A positive value moves the hole toward the left; a negative value moves it toward the right. Prefer the rim maker's specification.
physicalCorrections.rimOffsetInputNote: For an asymmetric rim, enter the rim bed's overall offset from the wheel centerline; use 0 for a symmetric rim. This is separate from the alternating-drilling offset.
physicalCorrections.holePairHelp: Enter the front and rear hub flange-hole diameters separately; common 14G spoke hubs are about 2.4–2.6 mm.
physicalCorrections.holeInputNote: Some hubs have no official CAD drawing, so the exact value cannot be confirmed directly. Some use a recessed counterbore or retention seat and some do not. Enter the actual hole value for J-bend; enter the value that matches the straight-pull structure. If official CAD already includes this detail, enter 0.
physicalCorrections.interlacingPairHelp: Set interlacing separately for the front and rear wheels; when enabled, enter a correction based on the actual spoke and hub structure.
physicalCorrections.interlacingInputNote: The correction is not a fixed value: for example, straight-gauge 2.0 mm round spokes, bladed spokes with different thicknesses, and butted spokes create different bend geometry. Hub exit direction can also change the angle. Most current hubs do not use interlacing, so the length effect is usually small; choose No when uncertain.
physicalCorrections.interlaceCompensationPlaceholder: Measured value; leave blank if unsure
physicalCorrections.elongationCompensationHelp: Leave blank to skip the manual correction; when filled, this value is subtracted for both wheels.
physicalCorrections.elongationGuideButton: Open the detailed model elongation guide
physicalCorrections.nipplePairHelp: Set the nipple type separately for the front and rear wheels; enter the actual length when using an internal nipple.
physicalCorrections.nippleInputNote: External nipples use the 14 mm SAPIM POLYAX as the length datum, so no extra length is entered. For internal nipples, enter the actual length from the model or official drawing; do not substitute the external 14 mm datum.
physicalCorrections.erdPairHelp: Enter the front and rear rim ERD values separately.
physicalCorrections.erdInputHelp: Enter the measured ERD in millimetres.
physicalCorrections.jBendHint: The spoke forms a hook at the flange hole.
physicalCorrections.straightPullHint: The spoke exits the hub slot in a straight line with no J-shaped bend.

parameter.title: Parameter definitions
parameter.intro: Use these definitions to double-check your rim and hub data before calculating. Small measurement differences can change the spoke length.

erd.title: ERD (Effective Rim Diameter)
erd.desc: The diameter at the spoke nipple seats inside the rim. Use the rim brand's ERD spec or measure it with two nipples and a caliper.

flangeDiameter.title: Flange diameter
flangeDiameter.desc: The circle diameter through the spoke hole centers on the hub flange (left and right can be different).

centerToFlange.title: Center-to-flange
centerToFlange.desc: The distance from the hub centerline to each flange (left and right). This affects dish and spoke length asymmetry.

holeCount.title: Spoke hole count
holeCount.desc: Must match both rim and hub (e.g. 24/28/32). Make sure you select the same count for front and rear.

crossPattern.title: Cross pattern
crossPattern.desc: How many times each spoke crosses other spokes (2x/3x/4x). Higher cross typically increases spoke length.

parameter.note: Tip: If you are unsure, use the manufacturer's published specs. If you measure yourself, measure twice and enter values to the same unit (mm).

workflow.title: Spoke length workflow
workflow.overviewAlt: Overview illustration for calculating bicycle spoke length
workflow.overviewCaption: Overview illustration showing which rim and hub measurements are needed to calculate bicycle spoke length.
workflow.stepOneFormulaValue: ERD = spoke 1 length + spoke 2 length + measured distance
stepOneItems: Prepare two old spokes of known length, two nipples, and a caliper.
Insert spokes through opposite holes in the rim.
Screw nipples until flush with the nipple groove bottom (ideal final position).
workflow.stepOneNote: * This method compensates for rim manufacturing tolerances.
workflow.stepOneAlt: Diagram showing how Effective Rim Diameter (ERD) is measured
workflow.stepOneCaption: Diagram showing how Effective Rim Diameter (ERD) is measured using two spokes, nipples and a caliper.
workflow.flangeDiameterBody: Use calipers to measure the distance between opposing spoke hole centers on the same flange.
workflow.centerToFlangeBody: Remove the hub axle if needed. Measure from the flange center to the hub centerline (or locknut face and subtract).
workflow.stepThreeBody: Enter measurements into the calculator. If the result is between standard sizes (e.g. 288.4mm), you usually round to the nearest available 1mm increment.
workflow.tipBody: Being 1mm longer is generally safer than 1mm shorter to ensure full thread engagement.
